name: Drum Kit Styles
author: Freek van Gool
description: Kits for Drum Kit in the most common styles: techno, house, trance, drum & bass, dubstep, hip-hop, funk & disco, electro, pop, rock, jazz and synthwave. Each kit combines instruments, sound models and a one-bar groove; techno has five kits. Loading a tune switches the device's own sequencer off, so you can audition the kit with your own sequencer; switch it back on to hear the groove stored in the tune. Drum and bass folders (around 172 to 176 BPM): Tech Step, Liquid DnB, Dancefloor DnB, Neurofunk, Jump Up, Jungle and Halftime DnB. Each kit has a two-bar groove in pattern A, a variation in B, a sparse breakdown in C and a snare-roll fill in D.
